newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe pledges debate on sexual equality.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe pledges debate on sexual equality.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe pledged on Wednesday to hold a parliamentary debate in coming weeks to discuss how to improve equality between men and women.
Juppe made the pledge after receving a report into equal opportunities from a watchdog committee chaired by parliamentarians Roselyne Bachelot and Gisele Halimi.
"I will now demand that National Assembly (lower house) organise a debate to study this question and see what laws, or constitutional reforms, should be adopted," Juppe said.
He did not detail possible measures but said he preferred voluntary measures to coercion.
The watchdog committee listed proposals including quotas for women, a referendum, a return to proportional representation and financial incentives for political parties recruiting women.
Although women make up 51.3 percent of the population, they hold only 5.5 percent of seats in the National Assembly (lower house) and 5.6 percent in the Senate.
